mcqs.question: What is ice?
mcqs.explanation: Ice is water in its solid state, meaning the water molecules are arranged in a fixed, rigid structure. Option B describes liquid water, C describes water vapour, and D describes dry ice (solid CO₂).

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes liquid water?

options.A: It has a fixed shape but no fixed volume
options.B: It takes the shape of its container and has a definite volume
options.C: It expands to fill any space

mcqs.answer: It takes the shape of its container and has a definite volume
mcqs.explanation: Liquid water flows to fill the bottom of any container, adopting its shape, while its volume remains constant. Option A describes a gas, C is also a gas property, and D is incorrect because liquid water is visible.

mcqs.question: Water vapour is best defined as:

options.C: Gaseous form of water invisible to the eye

mcqs.answer: Gaseous form of water invisible to the eye
mcqs.explanation: Water vapour is water in its gaseous state; the individual molecules are far apart and the gas is invisible. Option A describes frost, B describes mist or clouds, and D is not a recognized form of water.

mcqs.learning_point: Observable properties of the three states
mcqs.question: Which set correctly matches each state of water with its observable property?

options.A: Ice – takes shape of container, water – hard and rigid, vapour – visible droplets
options.B: Ice – hard and rigid, water – takes shape of container, vapour – invisible gas
options.C: Ice – invisible gas, water – hard and rigid, vapour – takes shape of container
options.D: Ice – expands when heated, water – contracts when cooled, vapour – solid at room temperature

mcqs.answer: Ice – hard and rigid, water – takes shape of container, vapour – invisible gas
mcqs.explanation: Ice is solid, so it is hard and keeps a fixed shape. Liquid water flows to fill its container. Water vapour is a gas and is invisible. All other options mix up these properties.

mcqs.learning_point: Water changing from one state to another
mcqs.question: When a glass of water is left uncovered on a hot day, which change of state occurs most directly?
mcqs.explanation: Heat causes water molecules at the surface to gain enough energy to escape as water vapour, which is evaporation. Freezing is the change to solid, melting is solid to liquid, and condensation is vapour to liquid, none of which happen directly in this scenario.

mcqs.question: A child places an ice cube on a warm kitchen counter. Which observation correctly describes what will happen to the ice cube?

options.A: It will melt and become liquid water
options.B: It will sublimate directly into water vapour
options.D: It will turn into solid carbon dioxide

mcqs.answer: It will melt and become liquid water
mcqs.explanation: At room temperature, ice absorbs heat and changes from solid to liquid – melting. Sublimation (direct solid to gas) occurs under specific low‑pressure conditions, not on a warm counter. The ice will not stay the same, and it cannot become solid CO₂.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about liquid water is NOT true?

options.A: It can exist at temperatures below 0°C under pressure
options.B: It takes the shape of its container

mcqs.explanation: Liquid water exists over a wide temperature range (0°C to 100°C at standard pressure). It is not always at its boiling point. Options A, B, and C correctly describe liquid water under certain conditions.

mcqs.question: Why does water vapour become invisible when it rises into the air?

options.B: Because it is in gaseous form with molecules far apart

mcqs.answer: Because it is in gaseous form with molecules far apart
mcqs.explanation: In the gaseous state, water molecules are spread out and do not scatter visible light, making the vapour invisible. Condensation (A) would make it visible as droplets, C describes freezing, and D is unrelated.
